identification.summary: Scarred Manticore is the name Check Point Research uses for an Iranian espionage actor, tracked in joint work with Sygnia's incident response team and described in an October 2023 report [S1]. Its main tool is LIONTAIL, a passive memory-resident backdoor framework for Windows servers made of custom shellcode loaders and memory-resident shellcode payloads. The implants call the HTTP.sys driver directly and use undocumented functions of it to pull payloads out of incoming HTTP requests, which lets traffic blend with normal web requests [S1][S2][S4]. The record's imported description also cites earlier IIS-based web shells, custom DLL backdoors and driver-based implants [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least 2019, per a summary of the Check Point report [S2]. Activity peaked in mid-2023 after going unnoticed for at least a year [S2][S3].
identification.notes: Cisco Talos tracks the same group as Shrouded Snooper [S2][S3]. One secondary summary says the group is most closely aligned with Microsoft's DEV-0861; this was not confirmed against a Microsoft primary source and no Microsoft name is recorded here [S7]. Check Point separates Scarred Manticore (espionage, initial access, data theft) from Void Manticore (aka Storm-0842, destructive operations); a Check Point comparison table reported via search snippet assigns them different roles in Albania [S8]. Do not merge the two clusters.

attribution.sponsor: Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS), as assessed by Check Point Research [S1][S2].
attribution.confidence: Check Point describes the actor as MOIS-affiliated [S1][S2]; the reports reviewed do not give a formal confidence level. Sources note some overlap of tools with OilRig-linked clusters but say direct attribution to OilRig is difficult [S2][S3]. No government attribution was found in the sources reviewed.
attribution.basis: Vendor analysis by Check Point Research and Sygnia: tool overlaps with previous MOIS-linked activity and with tooling seen in the Albanian government attacks [S1][S4][S5]. Underlying technical evidence was not directly reviewed (primary page could not be fetched) [S1].

objectives: Espionage against high-value Middle Eastern government and telecommunications organizations; researchers believe the primary goal is espionage, and the nature of the data stolen is not publicly known [S2][S3].

regions: Albania (government, as linked by tool overlap)
targeting.notes: Sector and country lists come from secondary coverage of the Check Point/Sygnia report [S2][S3][S5]. Reports differ on the Albania date: one outlet says 2021, another July 2022 [S2][S4][S5].

capabilities.summary: Targets Windows servers, with a long history of IIS-based backdoors, including custom web shells, custom DLL backdoors and driver-based implants [S1]. LIONTAIL is a passive backdoor framework: custom shellcode loaders, memory-resident shellcode payloads and a C backdoor that takes commands over HTTP; it uses undocumented HTTP.sys driver functions to hide in normal web requests [S2][S4]. Check Point states the framework is unique with no clear code overlap with known malware families [S2].

campaigns.summary: Some tools were observed in destructive ransomware and wiper attacks on Albanian government systems; outlets date this to 2021 or July 2022. Check Point attributes the destructive stage to a separate cluster (Void Manticore).

campaigns.summary: Campaign against government, military, telecom, IT, financial and NGO targets across Israel, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the UAE using the LIONTAIL framework; had been running undetected for at least a year.

diamond.adversary: MOIS-affiliated Iranian espionage actor per Check Point; also tracked by Talos as Shrouded Snooper [S1][S2].
diamond.capability: LIONTAIL passive HTTP.sys-based memory-resident backdoor framework, IIS web shells, DLL backdoors and driver implants [S1][S2][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised Windows/IIS servers act as passive listeners that receive commands in HTTP requests; actor C2 infrastructure details were not reviewed [S2][S4].
diamond.victim: Government, military, telecom, IT service, financial and NGO organizations in the Middle East [S2][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iranian state intelligence collection on regional governments and telecom providers, in a period of Iran-Israel and Iran-Gulf tension; the Albania link shows MOIS operations beyond the region [S1][S4].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing Windows servers running IIS/HTTP.sys, where memory-resident implants evade file-based detection [S2][S4].

gaps: Check Point's primary report and the Sygnia write-up could not be fetched (network resolution failed); findings rest on search-result summaries and secondary coverage [S1][S2].
Initial access vector, dwell times and individual victim identities were not established in the sources reviewed.
Microsoft naming is unconfirmed: one summary links the group to DEV-0861, but no Microsoft primary source was reviewed [S7].
Albania date conflict (2021 vs July 2022) and the exact division of roles between Scarred Manticore and Void Manticore need the primary Check Point text [S4][S5][S8].
No formal confidence level or government attribution located; OilRig overlap is described as tool overlap only [S2][S3].
No reporting after 2024 was found in the searches run; current activity status is unknown.
Press dates for S2-S7 are approximate to the month.
Removed unverified LIONHEAD/Israel email-exfiltration claim (S8 is about Void Manticore destructive activity) and unseen HivePro source S6.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Internet-facing Windows/IIS servers at government, telecom and IT-provider sites are key terrain, since the actor lives in HTTP.sys on these hosts [S1][S2]. STEP 2: Passive, memory-resident implants that hide inside normal HTTP traffic reduce network and file-based detection [S2][S4]. STEP 3: Template is compromise of an IIS server, installation of a passive HTTP.sys backdoor, then quiet collection of government and telecom data over long dwell [S2][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against Gulf and Levant government and telecom targets, including coalition partner hosts. MDCOA is the same access being handed to or reused by a destructive cluster, as the Albania overlap suggests [S4][S8]. Candidate indicators: unexpected modules or driver-level HTTP.sys registrations on IIS hosts, anomalous URL reservations, and web requests carrying embedded payloads to servers that normally see none [S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: add partner-nation telecom and government IIS servers to hunt priorities for coalition networks. (2) Authorities: server forensics on host-nation or contractor systems requires the owner's consent or agreements; plan early. (3) Mission assurance: memory-resident implants mean hunt teams need memory acquisition and HTTP.sys configuration review, not just file scanning [S2][S4]. (4) Coordination: Check Point and Sygnia are the originating reporters; coordinate with DC3 and partner CERTs, and treat espionage-to-destruction handoff as a planning risk [S1][S8].
